Instructions such as "open the drawer halfway, gently" depend on that physics: how far a part travels, how it resists, and what locks it. We present Open-World Law-to-Action (L2A). A vision-language model (VLM) proposes, for each movable part, its motions, the terms of its law of motion, and what may lock it. Each proposal becomes a...

items.summary: arXiv:2610.33715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of quantum computing into robotics requires mathematical representations that preserve the geometric structure and configuration dependence of robot motion. This paper introduces a structure-preserving quantum representation of rigid-body transformations and serial-manipulator kinematics, establishing a correspondence between classical kinematic models and parameterized quantum circuits. items.summary: arXiv:2610.33735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Floor traction influences wheel-slip behavior, dead-reckoning accuracy, and the navigation performance of wheeled mobile robots that rely on wheel odometry. items.summary: arXiv:2610.33794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying a language-guided navigation policy in a new building usually means watching it fail. items.summary: arXiv:2610.31789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. items.summary: arXiv:2610.31846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent agents should learn from their mistakes so that experience leads to continuous improvement. Yet today's agents recover from a mistake only temporarily: in-context reflections are easily forgotten across sessions and compete for limited context, while full-parameter fine-tuning is expensive and can interfere with existing capabilities. items.title: TACS-RF: Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave Modules
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the framework of TACS-RF - a Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave modules. items.title: BARC-Bench: Benign Asks, Risky Consequences
items.summary: arXiv:2610.32024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task instructions from users for agents are inherently underspecified, especially regarding safety boundaries--creating behavioral risks. items.summary: arXiv:2610.32057v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. items.summary: arXiv:2610.32127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a key technique for efficiently deploying large language models, as it compresses weights into low-bit representations without retraining. items.summary: arXiv:2610.32177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds.
